text:
lina: Quick sanity check — I'm about to apply a Terraform change that adds an IRSA annotation to the tenant namespace service account and wires ExternalSecrets to sync AWS creds into k8s. Plan looks harmless but want a quick peer review before I apply. TL;DR: adding eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn on sa tenant-uploader-sa in namespace tenant-prod, ExternalSecret will create secret tenant-aws-creds.

sam: Dump of the TF snippet? paste the exact annotation and the externalsecret source if you can.

lina: Sure, here's the important bits from the plan: 
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_service_account" "uploader" {
  metadata {
    name = "tenant-uploader-sa"
    namespace = "tenant-prod"
    annotations = {
      "eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn" = "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/tenant-prod-s3-uploader"
    }
  }
}

resource "external_secret" "tenant_aws" {
  metadata { name = "tenant-aws-creds" namespace = "tenant-prod" }
  spec { backendType = "aws" 
    data = [{ secretKey = "credentials" remoteRef = { key = "tenant/prod/s3" } }]
  }
}
```

mike: Couple quick checks: 1) make sure the IAM role (`tenant-prod-s3-uploader`) has the correct trust relation for the cluster OIDC provider (sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity) and the condition for the service account sub claim. 2) Confirm the role arn in TF matches the role created by our iam module (no typos in account id). 3) For ExternalSecrets, confirm it's pulling plaintext creds and not trying to mount as CSI volume unless you intended that.

sam: Also check the RoleBinding: if the sa needs any k8s permissions (list/get on pods or secrets) it has to be bound to a Role/ClusterRole. Are you relying on existing roles?

lina: We're only giving it S3 access via IAM; the pod only uses kubernetes API to read its own secret (no extra perms). The app reads the secret from k8s (tenant-aws-creds) mounted as env. So we have a Role that grants get/list on secrets in tenant-prod and a RoleBinding that binds tenant-uploader-sa to that Role.

jordan: I pulled the current k8s SA to verify: 
```yaml
# kubectl get sa tenant-uploader-sa -n tenant-prod -o yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: tenant-uploader-sa
  namespace: tenant-prod
  annotations: {}
secrets: []
automountServiceAccountToken: true
```
So annotation not yet present. After tf apply it'll update. automountServiceAccountToken true is OK — needed for projected token.

mike: Good. Two gotchas we've hit before: 
- external-secrets controller version mismatch where the AWS backend expects a different RemoteRef path — double-check the provider version in the cluster.
- If you have an OPA Gatekeeper or namespace mutating webhook that strips annotations, TF apply will succeed but the annotation may be removed at runtime. Any admission policies in tenant-prod?

lina: Not that I'm aware of for tenant-prod, but I'll check.

sam: Quick `terraform plan` lgtm? Can you paste the plan summary lines (resource changed: aws_iam_role, kubernetes_service_account, external_secret)?

lina: From plan summary: 
``
~ kubernetes_service_account.uploader (update)
~ external_secret.tenant_aws (create)
= aws_iam_role.tenant_prod_s3 (no-op)
```
We already created the role in an earlier PR, so TF just references it.

jordan: If role exists, confirm the role's trust policy includes the OIDC provider for the cluster: 
`Condition: StringEquals: {"sts:sub": "system:serviceaccount:tenant-prod:tenant-uploader-sa"}`
If it matches, IRSA should work.

mike: One more micro-check: when ExternalSecrets creates `tenant-aws-creds`, ensure it doesn't set ownerReferences to a resource that gets pruned by our cleanup jobs. We had a case where ephemeral resources got GC'd. Use namespace-scoped secret without owner refs.

lina: Good catch — ES spec is set to template the secret with no owner refs. Will verify post-apply.

infra-bot: terraform-plan: passed for branch feature/tenant-irsa-bind — no drift detected. :white_check_mark:

sam: If infra-bot says plan passed and role trust looks correct, I'd be fine with apply. Maybe run `kubectl describe sa tenant-uploader-sa -n tenant-prod` after apply to ensure annotation is present.

lina: Will do. I'll wait ~30m for any objections then apply. Thanks all :pray: 

mike: :+1: @lina do a quick smoke by deploying the app to a canary pod and verify it can access S3 and secret is present.

lina: Will run canary and post results here.

(30 minutes later) lina: applying now, will update with canary results.

(35 minutes later) lina: Canary done — pod started, secret env present, `aws s3 ls s3://tenant-prod-bucket` succeeded using assumed role. Annotation visible on SA. All good. :tada:
